channel.title: Wire — tech digest
channel.description: One digest a day, merged from thirty sources.

item.title: A look at the math that OpenAI claims computes faster Fourier transforms
item.description: The OpenAI algorithm for the FFT is less a breakthrough and more a malicious exploit. (2 sources: hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: AI models can provably hide arbitrary capabilities
item.description: Abstract page for arXiv paper 2610.13928: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: AI is a tool and using it well takes skill
item.description: A response to Rich Hickey's "'AI' is Not a Tool": automation and tool use can coexist, and wielding an LLM well requires skill, feedback, and judgment. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Intel D270 GPU AI Accelerator–Up to 480 GB LPDDR5X
item.description: Intel GPU D270 is an inference-optimized data center GPU built for agentic AI, long contexts, and high-concurrency serving at practical power and cost. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Janas: Run LLMs larger than RAM by streaming experts from SSD
item.description: 37 tok/s from Qwen3-Next-80B (48 GB) on a 32 GB laptop, 24 without drafts vs 2.8 for llama.cpp; reading 62 vs 16 tok/s. Faster than llama.cpp on all 13 models compared in Q4_K_M. LLMs bigger than your RAM, pure C, CPU or GPU. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Production Patterns for Agents, Evals, and LLM Costs: QCon AI New York 2026
item.description: Once AI is in production, code arrives faster than it can be reviewed, token costs rise, evals have to be good enough to act on, and agents need permissions and guardrails. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Import AI 476: Creativity and RSI; worse-than-China open weight models; AI goes to space
item.description: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe. (1 source: importai)

item.title: 2026 in LLMs (so far)
item.description: In 2026, autonomous agents escaped their sandboxes to accidentally cyberattack government infrastructure. Now that AI writes the boilerplate, developers are paradoxically left battling only the most grueling, high-stakes problems. (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: AWS Reworks EventBridge Custom Buses for Enterprise-Scale Event-Driven Architectures
item.description: AWS has introduced an enhanced Custom Event Bus for Amazon EventBridge, targeting a problem that often emerges when event-driven architectures move beyond a single team or AWS account: the event infrastructure itself becomes fragmented. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Cloudflare’s OHTTP Gateway Refuses to Decrypt Requests That Arrive Through Cloudflare
item.description: Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of its OHTTP Gateway, a managed endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP requests for an origin. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Amazon CloudFront now supports AWS Lambda Web Functions as an origin
item.description: Starting today, you can deliver web applications built on AWS Lambda Web Functions through CloudFront's global edge network. (1 source: aws)

item.title: Amazon EC2 G7 instances now available in Europe (Frankfurt) and Europe (Stockholm) Regions
item.description: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) G7 instances powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs are now available in Europe (Frankfurt) and Europe (Stockholm) Regions. (1 source: aws)

item.title: Amazon Connect Customer now prefills step-by-step guides for after contact work
item.description: Amazon Connect Customer can now fill in the step-by-step guides that agents complete after a contact, using information extracted from customer conversations, such as booking identifiers, claim numbers, and conversation summaries. (1 source: aws)

item.title: AWS Lambda announces Lambda Web Functions
item.description: AWS Lambda announces Lambda Web Functions, a new serverless compute primitive where your code handles HTTP requests directly. Your code listens on a port and handles requests as it would on any HTTP server. (1 source: aws)
